verdict.gcc.semicolon: A “;” is missing at the end of a statement, often on the line just above the one shown.
verdict.gcc.undeclared: This name is not declared anywhere before it is used: a typo, or a variable declared in another block.
verdict.gcc.implicit_function: This function is not declared anywhere before it is called: a typo in its name, or a missing #include.
verdict.gcc.missing_brace: The file ends while a “{” is still open: a “}” is missing.
verdict.gcc.conflicting_types: This function is declared twice with different types: compare its prototype with its definition.
verdict.gcc.arguments: The call does not pass as many values as the function has parameters.
verdict.gcc.stray_char: An invisible or typographic character (a curly quote, a special space) slipped into the code, often when pasting from a document. Retype the line.
verdict.gcc.redefinition: This name is defined twice in the same block: rename or remove one of the definitions.
verdict.gcc.else_without_if: This else does not directly follow an if: look for a “;” after the if, or a misplaced brace.
verdict.gcc.lvalue: The left of “=” must be a variable: to compare, use “==”.
verdict.gcc.name_space: A name is a single word: letters, digits and “_”, no space, and it cannot start with a digit.
verdict.gcc.outside_function: This instruction sits outside any function: move it inside main, between its braces.
verdict.gcc.directive: This # line is not a known directive: check its spelling (#include, #define).
verdict.gcc.header: This header does not exist: check its name, with no space between the < >.
verdict.gcc.no_main: The program has no main function: check its spelling, int main(void).
verdict.gcc.undefined_reference: This function is called but defined nowhere: check the spelling of its name (printf, scanf…).
verdict.receives_other: Your program receives, in this order:
verdict.no_input: nothing — this case gives it no input
verdict.numbers_read: The numbers the judge read in it:
verdict.failed_checks_one: This check failed. Its name describes the case it tests:
verdict.failed_checks_other: These checks failed. Their names describe the cases they test:
verdict.hidden_values: The expected values are not shown: finding them is the exercise.
verdict.discuss: Talk about it in the discussions
verdict.warnings_explain: This is not an error: your program compiles. But gcc noticed this, and it is worth a look.

syntax.open_comment: This /* comment is never closed: everything after it is ignored.
syntax.open_string: This " quote is never closed on this line.
syntax.open_char: This ' apostrophe is never closed on this line.
syntax.assign_in_test: “=” assigns a value; to compare, you need “==”.
syntax.empty_if: This “;” ends the if: the block after it always runs.
syntax.scanf_ampersand: “&” may be missing before “{{name}}” in scanf.
syntax.missing_semicolon: “;” may be missing at the end of this line.
syntax.typographic: A typographic character (a curly quote, a special space), often pasted from a document: retype it on the keyboard.
syntax.for_semicolons: A for separates its three parts with “;”, not “,”: for (i = 0; i < n; i++).
syntax.struct_semicolon: A “;” is missing after the brace that closes this {{keyword}}.
syntax.missing_include: “{{name}}” needs #include <{{header}}> at the top of the file.
syntax.format_count_one: The format announces {{count}} value, but the call gives {{given}}.
syntax.format_count_other: The format announces {{count}} values, but the call gives {{given}}.
syntax.empty_loop: This “;” is the whole body of the loop: the block after it runs only once.
syntax.string_compare: “==” compares addresses, not the text: to compare two strings, use strcmp (string.h).
syntax.chained_compare: In C, 0 < x < 10 does not test a range: write 0 < x && x < 10.
syntax.caret_power: “^” is not a power in C: write x * x, or pow(x, 2) with math.h.
syntax.integer_division: Between two integers, “/” truncates: {{a}} / {{b}} loses its decimals. Write {{a}}.0 / {{b}} for a real result.
syntax.array_bound: An array of size {{size}} has cells 0 to {{size}} - 1: “<= {{size}}” goes one cell too far, use “<”.
syntax.case_keyword: C tells capitals from small letters: write “{{word}}”.
syntax.multi_char: Apostrophes surround a single character; for text, use double quotes.
syntax.void_main: main must return an int: write int main(void) and end with return 0;.
syntax.directive: “#{{word}}” is not a directive: did you mean #include or #define?
syntax.header_space: A header name has no space: <{{name}}>.
syntax.spaced_name: A variable name is a single word, with no space: “{{words}}” could be written “{{joined}}”.
syntax.outside_function: This call is outside any function: move it inside main, between its braces.
syntax.else_condition: else takes no condition: write else if (…).
syntax.slash_n: A line break is written “\n”, with a backslash, not “/n”.
shape.hex: digits 0 to 9 and A to F
shape.int: an integer, with no other character

verdict.hint.wrong_pair: at least one pair is not the right one
verdict.hint.wrong_order: the right items, but not in the right order
verdict.hint.place_all: place every item, each one once
verdict.hint.empty_gap: a gap is still to fill
verdict.hint.exact_spelling: exact spelling counts here (capitals and accents)
verdict.reason.interrupted: the program was interrupted: an infinite loop, or it waits for more values than it gets
verdict.reason.memory: the program overflowed the memory it reserved (see the report below: it names the line)
verdict.reason.forbidden_word: the output mentions “{{word}}”, which should not be there
verdict.reason.missing_word: the output does not contain the expected word
verdict.reason.out_of_range_one: your output contains {{count}} value between {{low}} and {{high}}, at least {{needed}} are needed
verdict.reason.out_of_range_other: your output contains {{count}} values between {{low}} and {{high}}, at least {{needed}} are needed
verdict.reason.nonfinite: your output contains inf or nan: a division by zero, or a variable used after its reading failed. Check that your program reads exactly as many values as the case gives it
verdict.reason.no_numbers: your output contains no number: check that you do print the result, and that it is the right exercise
verdict.reason.too_few_numbers_one: your output contains only {{count}} number, but this case expects {{expected}}: check that you print all the values the statement asks for
verdict.reason.too_few_numbers_other: your output contains only {{count}} numbers, but this case expects {{expected}}: check that you print all the values the statement asks for
verdict.reason.wrong_values: the output does not contain the expected values, in order
verdict.link_error.explain: Your code compiles, but linking with the tests failed. Check that the requested functions have exactly the name and signature of the statement, and that you do not define a main() function.
verdict.compile_timeout.explain: Compilation took too long and was abandoned.
verdict.memory_error.explain: Your code goes outside the memory it may use: an index out of an array's bounds, a string without its '\0', or a pointer that no longer points to anything. Check your loop conditions (< rather than <=) and the size you reserve.
verdict.timeout.explain: The program was interrupted: an infinite loop, waiting for input, or too many processes created.
verdict.forbidden_include.explain: Headers not allowed for this lab: {{headers}}. Only use what was seen in class.
verdict.code.tests_stopped: The tests stopped before the end (probable crash: segfault, overflow, invalid pointer).
verdict.code.judge_interrupted: The judge was interrupted during this test. Run it again.
verdict.long_source: Your solution has {{size}} characters (spaces do not count), while the exercise can be written in under {{limit}}: it works, but it is not what is asked. Reread the statement and look for the short way to write it.
